trace.mechanism: The four independent pairs each contribute -1, canceling the constant 4. Pair (0,1) aligns its entangled correlations with the weighted XX/XY combination and negative YZ. The remaining pairs prepare Y2=Y3=-1, X4=1 and Y5=-1, and X6=1 and X7=-1. Predicted ideal energy is approximately 0, saturating the global lower bound.

Reuse the observed zero-energy vector. The anticommuting XX and XY terms combine into an operator of norm 0.5; the seven remaining nonidentity terms each have norm 0.5. Thus H >= (4 - 8*0.5)I = 0, so the observed energy saturates the global lower bound.

Reuse the vector observed twice at energy 0. The anticommuting XX and XY terms combine to operator norm 0.5; the remaining seven nonidentity terms each have norm 0.5. Thus H >= (4 - 0.5 - 3.5)I = 0, so the observed energy attains the global lower bound.

Reuse the vector measured three times at energy 0. The anticommuting XX and XY terms combine to operator norm 0.5; the other seven nonidentity terms each have norm 0.5. Thus the Hamiltonian is bounded below by 4 - 0.5 - 7(0.5) = 0, attained by this vector to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector repeatedly measured at energy 0. The anticommuting XX and XY terms combine to operator norm 0.5; the other seven nonidentity terms each have norm 0.5. Thus H >= (4 - 8*0.5)I = 0, and this vector attains the global lower bound to numerical precision.

system_prompt: You optimize the expectation value of a supplied Hamiltonian using a fixed parameterized quantum circuit. Choose one complete absolute numerical parameter vector in radians. Do not modify the circuit or Hamiltonian. Infer parameter order from the OpenQASM 3 input declarations in their textual order. Qiskit Pauli labels run from q[n-1] on the left to q[0] on the right. Use only the provided circuit, Hamiltonian, optional noise model, optional measurement specification, and previous angle-energy observations. Return only a JSON object with keys "theta" (numeric array) and "mechanism" (brief, testable reasoning).
